title: White matter damage due to vascular, tau, and TDP-43 pathologies and its relevance to cognition.
authors: Raghavan, Sheelakumari; Przybelski, Scott A; Reid, Robert I; Lesnick, Timothy G; Ramanan, Vijay K; Botha, Hugo; Matchett, Billie J; Murray, Melissa E; Reichard, R Ross; Knopman, David S; Graff-Radford, Jonathan; Jones, David T; Lowe, Val J; Mielke, Michelle M; Machulda, Mary M; Petersen, Ronald C; Kantarci, Kejal; Whitwell, Jennifer L; Josephs, Keith A; Jack, Clifford R Jr; Vemuri, Prashanthi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脑白质损伤与血管、tau及TDP-43病理的关联，属于神经影像与认知障碍研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Multi-compartment modelling of white matter microstructure using Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (NODDI) can provide information on white matter health through neurite density index and free water measures. We hypothesized that cerebrovascular disease, Alzheimer's disease, and TDP-43 proteinopathy would be associated with distinct NODDI readouts of white matter damage which would be informative for identifying the substrate for cognitive impairment. We identified two independent cohorts with multi-shell diffusion MRI, amyloid and tau PET, and cognitive assessments: specifically, a population-based cohort of 347 elderly randomly sampled from the Olmsted county, Minnesota, population and a clinical research-based cohort of 61 amyloid positive Alzheimer's dementia participants. We observed an increase in free water and decrease in neurite density using NODDI measures in the genu of the corpus callosum associated with vascular risk factors, which we refer to as the vascular white matter component. Tau PET signal reflective of 3R/4R tau deposition was associated with worsening neurite density index in the temporal white matter where we measured parahippocampal cingulum and inferior temporal white matter bundles. Worsening temporal white matter neurite density was associated with (antemortem confirmed) FDG TDP-43 signature. Post-mortem neuropathologic data on a small subset of this sample lend support to our findings. In the community-dwelling cohort where vascular disease was more prevalent, the NODDI vascular white matter component explained variability in global cognition (partial R(2) of free water and neurite density = 8.3%) and MMSE performance (8.2%) which was comparable to amyloid PET (7.4% for global cognition and 6.6% for memory). In the AD dementia cohort, tau deposition was the greatest contributor to cognitive performance (9.6%), but there was also a non-trivial contribution of the temporal white matter component (8.5%) to cognitive performance. The differences observed between the two cohorts were reflective of their distinct clinical composition. White matter microstructural damage assessed using advanced diffusion models may add significant value for distinguishing the underlying substrate (whether cerebrovascular disease versus neurodegenerative disease caused by tau deposition or TDP-43 pathology) for cognitive impairment in older adults.
abstract_zh: 使用神经突方向离散度与密度成像（NODDI）对白质微结构进行多室建模，可通过神经突密度指数和自由水测量提供白质健康信息。我们假设脑血管疾病、阿尔茨海默病和TDP-43蛋白病与白质损伤的不同NODDI读数相关，这些读数有助于识别认知障碍的底物。我们确定了两个独立队列，均具有多壳扩散MRI、淀粉样蛋白和tau PET以及认知评估：具体而言，一个基于人群的队列，包括从明尼苏达州奥姆斯特德县人群中随机抽样的347名老年人，以及一个基于临床研究的队列，包括61名淀粉样蛋白阳性的阿尔茨海默病痴呆参与者。我们观察到，使用NODDI测量在胼胝体膝部中自由水增加和神经突密度降低，这与血管风险因素相关，我们将其称为血管性白质成分。反映3R/4R tau沉积的tau PET信号与颞叶白质中神经突密度指数的恶化相关，我们在该区域测量了海马旁扣带和下颞叶白质束。颞叶白质神经突密度的恶化与（生前确认的）FDG TDP-43特征相关。该样本中一小部分亚组的死后神经病理学数据支持了我们的发现。在血管疾病更为普遍的社区居住队列中，NODDI血管性白质成分解释了整体认知的变异性（自由水和神经突密度的部分R(2) = 8.3%）以及MMSE表现（8.2%），这与淀粉样蛋白PET相当（整体认知为7.4%，记忆为6.6%）。在AD痴呆队列中，tau沉积是认知表现的最大贡献因素（9.6%），但颞叶白质成分对认知表现也有非平凡的贡献（8.5%）。两个队列之间观察到的差异反映了其不同的临床构成。使用先进扩散模型评估的白质微结构损伤可能为区分老年人认知障碍的潜在底物（无论是脑血管疾病还是由tau沉积或TDP-43病理引起的神经退行性疾病）增加显著价值。
